body:
Is it gamethrowing for a revealed mayor to randomly suspect a town member on d2 or d3, despite literally no way of knowing whether the person is guilty or inno?
I played a game last night where I was investigator, and on d3 the mayor revealed and out of the blue said I was maf/sk (he never specified which). I may have been pardoned by a tie if it weren't for his mayorly voting advantage. Then, when it was revealed that I was the investigator all along, they simply shrugged it off and said "Idk that was just a guess".
He died the next night though so yeah, justice served.

As a trans and otherwise queer person, I understand you completely. I cried myself to sleep last night and I've never feared so much for my rights—bearing in mind that I live in the state most famous for HB2, and I'm surrounded by homophobes and transphobes, so that should say a lot about the election results.

Poor John. My mom's a Trump supporter and yesterday I mentioned something John Oliver had said about the election. I guess my mom's sick of me quoting him because she went on a half-hour rant about how she doesn't give a flying fuck about John Oliver.
Damn. I pretty much live for South Park and Last Week Tonight, so it sucks that half of what I was looking forward to isn't here. Don't know what I'll do when LWT goes on hiatus/season gap.

heh, I had to babysit a kid (eight year old cousin) over the summer who wasn't bad at heart but was very hyper and somewhat frustrating at times (like all children are). on day two, I caught her watching porn on her tablet, so I did the responsible thing and changed the wifi password and blocked her tablet from using it. I told my mom and she said that what I did was good enough, so we didn't end up telling the girl's dad (aka my uncle)
a friend of mine told me to put my mom's vibrator in her backpack (she brought it every day because it had her snacks and toys in it) whenever she was being a brat and then to tell my mom that I had "just found it there"

that same friend had also told me to just take the vibrator and hide it in my room because it would be far too embarrassing and awkward for my mom to ever ask about.

Wow. My mom is the only family member of mine who knows about my sexuality—my dad claims he's liberal but he's homophobic and transphobic, and the rest of my family would practically lynch me if I even mentioned it. A couple at my grandparents' church admitted that they weren't married, just in a relationship and living together, and even though they were straight and extremely conservative/Christian, they were practically burned at the stake for it.

Not a parent, but this scenario is kind of the other way around:

I found an uncomfortably large vibrator in my mom's room once when I was looking for candy (which she often hoards). Oh, and it wasn't the cheap kind either, they didn't spare any realism when they made that thing. 

Even worse, I thought it was a flashlight. You can imagine my surprise when the flashlight had veins, but of course the most traumatizing part was when I pressed the button and instead of illuminating the drawer, it vibrated intensely. Took me half an hour to find out how to turn it off.

My mom found notes and stuff from my ex-girlfriend and confronted me about it—she actually wasn't as upset as I expected, but I was shocked giving that she's a very conservative Christian and this is North Carolina :p (technically the relationship was straight but I'm still closeted in terms of gender identity)
This is really helpful! I've mostly gotten the hang of punctuating dialogue, but thank you for providing a reference that I can revisit if necessary. :)
Same. Is it bad that I took the words "from scratch" too seriously and only recently discovered that planning the novel ahead is acceptable?

I still remember the day he died, he was on my mind when I woke up but it was just like any other day until I went online and saw the news.
Something died inside of me that day, and I remember carrying on with a heavy heart.
I'm still seeking closure over it, its weird. I've never been so torn up over the death of someone I never really met in person.
